acceptance_criteria.criterion: [data-theme="dark"] block exists immediately after the :root block and resets all 8 color variables (--color-bg, --color-surface, --color-border, --color-text, --color-text-muted, --color-header-bg, --color-header-text, --shadow).
A commented hardcoded-hex overrides section exists at the bottom of styles.css covering all 16 selectors listed in the plan (badge variants, table hover, error/success/reset banners, health badges).
select and input[type="text"] elements within .filter-bar and .insights-filters receive explicit color and background overrides in the dark block.
.theme-toggle button styles exist with ::before content swap: 🌙 in light mode, ☀️ in dark mode.
No existing light-mode styles are removed or broken.

summary: Implemented dark mode for the MCP Server Dashboard GUI across all three frontend files with zero new dependencies and no build step.

styles.css: Added [data-theme="dark"] variable override block immediately after :root (8 variables). Added .theme-toggle button with ::before content swap (🌙/☀️). Appended hardcoded-hex overrides section covering all 16 selectors: badge variants, table hover, error/success/reset banners, health badges, and filter-bar select/input controls.

index.html: Added FOUC-prevention inline <script> in <head> that synchronously applies data-theme="dark" before first paint (unless localStorage explicitly stores 'light'). Added <button id="theme-toggle"> with aria-label in nav.

app.js: Added Theme IIFE module (section 2) before Router. Implements init() — reads localStorage, defaults to dark, wires click listener on toggle button; toggle() — flips attribute and persists to localStorage. Bootstrap section now calls Theme.init() before Router.init().

comments.note: No observations — code is clean and consistent. All changes follow the established zero-build-step, plain-JS SPA pattern. The Theme IIFE matches the style of the existing API and Router IIFEs.

summary: All 5 acceptance criteria verified against source files. [data-theme="dark"] block at styles.css L38-47 immediately follows :root, resets all 8 CSS variables. Hardcoded-hex overrides section at L1183-1255 covers all 16 selectors (badge-ready, badge-in-progress, badge-in_progress, badge-complete, badge-blocked, tbody tr:hover, error-banner, success-banner, reset-modal-banner, reset-stage-present, reset-stage-missing, health-badge, health-badge.healthy, health-badge.attention, filter-bar select + insights-filters select, filter-bar input[type="text"]). .insights-filters confirmed to contain only select elements (no input[type="text"]), so combined select override is sufficient. .theme-toggle::before content swap verified at L1171-1177 (🌙 in light, ☀️ in dark). FOUC prevention inline script in <head> defaults to dark unless localStorage stores 'light'. localStorage key 'mcp-theme' consistent across FOUC script and Theme IIFE. Theme.init() called before Router.init() in bootstrap. No existing light-mode styles removed or broken — only additive changes.

comments.note: FOUC prevention is solid — the synchronous inline script in <head> runs before first paint, so no flash even on default-dark load. The 'mcp-theme' localStorage key is used consistently in both the FOUC script (index.html) and the Theme IIFE (app.js), avoiding any key mismatch bug.
The .insights-filters container only renders select elements (confirmed in app.js L1268-1282), so the absence of an insights-filters input[type="text"] dark override is correct by design, not a gap.

summary: Reviewed all three modified files: mcp-server/gui/public/styles.css, index.html, app.js. Implementation is clean, minimal, and architecturally consistent.

styles.css: [data-theme="dark"] variable block correctly placed immediately after :root, all 8 variables overridden with appropriate dark-palette values. theme-toggle ::before content swap uses correct Unicode escapes (\1F319 for 🌙, \2600\FE0F for ☀️). Hardcoded-hex overrides section well-organised with descriptive comments, covers all 16 required selectors. filter-bar and insights-filters form controls receive correct background/color overrides. No existing styles removed.

index.html: FOUC-prevention inline script correctly placed in <head> after the stylesheet link, runs synchronously before first paint, defaults to dark unless 'light' is explicitly stored. Toggle button correctly carries id, class, and initial aria-label (which is immediately overridden by _apply() on init — not a bug).

app.js: Theme IIFE follows the established section structure (API=1, Theme=2, Router=3). STORAGE_KEY constant 'mcp-theme' matches the FOUC script exactly. _apply() correctly uses setAttribute/removeAttribute rather than setting a 'light' attribute, keeping light mode as the attribute-absent default. Null-guards on _toggleBtn prevent errors if DOM is missing. toggle() reads current state from the DOM attribute — correct, not stale state. Bootstrap calls Theme.init() before Router.init(), ensuring theme is applied before any route-driven rendering. All acceptance criteria confirmed met.

comments.note: index.html theme-toggle has a static aria-label="Toggle dark mode" that is immediately replaced by Theme._apply() on init. Not a bug — JS runs synchronously before user interaction — but if JS were to fail, the static label is semantically vague. Negligible risk for an internal dashboard.

styles.css [data-theme="dark"] tbody tr:hover background uses var(--color-surface). In light mode the hover is handled elsewhere (likely a near-white tint). The dark override using --color-surface (dark card background) is a sensible and deliberate choice — rows show the card-level background on hover rather than a potentially harsh contrast colour.

\2600\FE0F (☀️) in CSS content uses a variation selector (U+FE0F) for emoji presentation. This is technically correct and functions across all modern browsers. Older or atypical rendering agents may show the text variant ☀ instead; acceptable trade-off for an internal tool.

No observations beyond the above — overall code quality is high. The Theme IIFE cleanly mirrors the existing API and Router module pattern. Zero new dependencies, no build step, no regression risk identified.
